transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this pre-job review together because we need to discuss the solvent-recovery trial for the skid beside the coating area. As you know, we have nine hundred liters of solvent mixture in drums awaiting a disposition decision, and before I can authorize any trial run on production solvent, plant policy requires us to go through this review with process engineering, maintenance, and environmental compliance present. I also need to confirm that we've satisfied every element of the standard pre-job procedure: equipment inspection, closed transfer, ventilation verification, vapor monitoring, and documented waste handling. So let's start by hearing from each of you on where we stand. Process engineering — can you walk us through the current status of the skid and whether it's ready for a production solvent trial?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to share an important finding from a bench compatibility test I completed yesterday. The test shows that only 600 liters of the stored solvent mixture is suitable for this skid. The remaining 300 liters contains a solvent component that the skid's seals are not rated for. This result is still in my lab notebook and hasn't been uploaded to the process file yet, but it's critical for our disposition decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share my pre-use inspection findings. During my inspection of the solvent-recovery skid, I found that the transfer pump seal must be replaced and pressure-tested before the skid can be operated. The replacement takes exactly 3 hours, and the seal kit is already in the maintenance storeroom. I recorded this finding on a paper inspection sheet, but it has not yet been entered into the electronic work-order system. So from a maintenance standpoint, the skid is not currently ready for operation — we need to complete this seal replacement and pressure test first.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share critical information from my permit review. I received clarification from the environmental office this morning. This solvent recovery operation requires ventilation of at least 6 air changes per hour, exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors, and a hazardous-waste manifest for the incompatible 300 liters. I have not yet filed this permitting clarification with the trial paperwork, so it's important we get this on the record now. Notably, the 300 liters that Jonas just identified as incompatible aligns with the hazardous-waste manifest requirement I was informed of.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Thank you all for bringing these findings forward — this is exactly why we do pre-job reviews. Let me summarize where we stand against the standard pre-job procedure before I make my decision. First, from Jonas: the bench compatibility test shows only 600 liters of the 900 is suitable for this skid, and 300 liters contains a component the skid's seals aren't rated for. Jonas, I need that result uploaded to the process file as soon as possible — it's critical to the disposition decision. Second, from Priya: the transfer pump seal must be replaced and pressure-tested before operation, which takes 3 hours, and the seal kit is already on hand. That means the equipment inspection element is not yet satisfied. Priya, please get that paper inspection sheet into the electronic work-order system and schedule the seal replacement and pressure test. Third, from Caleb: the environmental office has specified 6 air changes per hour ventilation, 2 continuously operating LEL monitors, and a hazardous-waste manifest for the incompatible 300 liters. That covers ventilation verification, vapor monitoring, and part of documented waste handling — but the manifest for the 300 liters still needs to be prepared and filed. So to be clear: I cannot authorize the trial today. We have unresolved items on equipment readiness, documentation, and waste handling. Once the seal is replaced and pressure-tested, the compatibility data is uploaded, the ventilation and LEL monitor requirements are verified in place, and the hazardous-waste manifest for the 300 liters of incompatible solvent is prepared, I will reconsider authorization for a trial on the compatible 600 liters only. Are there any questions or anything else anyone needs to add before we close out this review?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Understood, Mara. I'll upload the compatibility test results to the process file today. One question: should I also label or segregate the 300 liters of incompatible solvent in the drums so there's no risk of it being mistakenly included in the trial run once authorization is granted for the compatible 600 liters?
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Good question from Jonas on segregating the incompatible 300 liters — I'd support that as a practical safeguard. From my side, Mara, I'll get the paper inspection sheet entered into the electronic work-order system today and schedule the seal replacement and pressure test. Since the seal kit is already in the maintenance storeroom, I can start the 3-hour replacement immediately after the work order is created. Once the new seal is installed, I'll run the pressure test to confirm integrity before we consider the skid ready. I'll report back once the pressure test passes.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Priya. From my side, I want to make sure we're clear on the environmental compliance items that still need to be closed out before Mara can reconsider authorization. First, I still need to file the permitting clarification I received this morning with the trial paperwork — I'll do that today so it's officially on record. Second, regarding the hazardous-waste manifest for the 300 liters of incompatible solvent: once Jonas segregates and labels those drums, I can begin preparing the manifest so that the documented waste handling element is fully satisfied. Third, on ventilation and vapor monitoring — the requirements are 6 air changes per hour and exactly 2 continuously operating LEL monitors. I'll need confirmation from maintenance or facilities that the ventilation rate is verified and that both LEL monitors are installed, operational, and set for continuous monitoring before the trial proceeds. To Jonas's question — yes, I'd strongly support segregating and labeling the 300 liters as incompatible. That segregation will also support the hazardous-waste manifest process, since those 300 liters will need to be handled as a separate waste stream. I'll report back once the permitting clarification is filed and the manifest preparation is underway.
